div.head: PLAINTIFF NON-SUITED.
div.p: PLAINTIFF NON-SUITED.

On Thursday, in the County Court, hi- Honour Judge Barnard I;ailey, K.C.: gave judgment in an action of Roger v. Owen, which had been heard at the previous sitting, on November 2nd. It was an action to recover 5:58 10s. under a business purchase agreement, the plaintiff being Mr. George Roger, Bridge Foot, Warrington, and the defendant, Mr. Peter Owen, who formerly carried on a similar busi- ness under the name of "Stockton and Lee," at Berkshire-street, Miles Platting, Manchester. Mr. Browne appeared for the plaintiff, and Mr. Gilbert Jordan (instructed by Messrs. Richard Higham and Co., Manchester), for the defend- ant.

In July, 1915, an oral agreement for the sale of the Manchester business .was entered into be- tween the parties, and this was confirmed by a written document in the following October. The business was transferred to Warrington, and in March last one of the 'work girls, Annie Salisbury, was injured by an accident. Her claim under the Workmen's Compensation' Act was settled by plaintiff for £53 ss. and £5 ss. costs, and his contention now was that an in- surance policy standing in defendant's name was transferred to him under the agreement, and that he should be indemnified against the sums mentioned. The defendant's case was that, the agreement made no mention of any obligation on the part of the defendant to transfer the policy, that an assignment of the policy would not bind the insurance company, and, further, that the insurance only covered contingencies in the Manchester business.
It transpired during the bearing of the case that while premiums on the policy had been paid, the policy itself had gone astray and could not be found. ."

. In giving judgment in favour of the defendant on Thursday; his Honour reviewed the facts, and said :—" I find there was an oral agreement contemporaneous with the oral agreement for sale with the plaintiff, and for the benefit of the defendant's interest in the policy in queks- tion. In my opinion this agreement did not operate to bind defendant to procure the con- sent of the insurance company, without which the transfer could not have been effected in law; but at the utmost to do or concur in doing at the request of plaintiff all in his power by way of assignment, declaration of trust, or other- wise. to.bring about such transfer. If this view is erroneous and the fact of the orll agreement was to. bring defendant under a positive obliga- tion to procure the company's assent, this does not avail the plaintiff, \for even with a hill effective transfer of the defendant's interest he would still have been unable to recover against the company. the loss he sustained in conse- quence of the accident, for the defendant's in- surance was against accidents to workpeople employed in Manchester, and nowhere else. I do not find that defendant failed to do any act he undertook to do, and in any case it is clear the damage claimed did not flow from a breach of agreement to transfer." His Honour, there- fore, dismissed the action with costs to de_ fendant, and granted a stay of execution for fourteen days.

div.head: FULL BATTALION PROPHESIED.
div.p: A FULL BATTALION PROPHESIED.

Last week Colonel Formby, officer commanding the Liverpool group of battalions, Lancashire Volunteer Regiment, paid an informal visit to the headquarters of the Warrington Company. In company with Capt. Johnson and Capt. Rylands (O:C.. Warrington Company). he arrived at the Drill Hall shortly' after_ 8 o'clock, and was introduced to the officers on parade. Platoons Nos. 3 and 4, about 100 strong, under Company-Sergt.-Major Sullivan, went through a number of company movements in smart style, and Colonel Formby, in address- ing the N.C.O.'s, complimented them on their large increase in strength, and expressed his satisfaction with what he had seen. He said that when recently speaking to a well-known Warrington officer (Col. Edelsten) he mentioned the small numbers in the company, and Col. Edelsten replied, " Wait ! When Warrington is asked, a full battalion will be the result. I know Warrington !" He (Col. Formby) was now convinced that Col. Edelsten was right.

div.head: WOUNDED SOLDIERS.
div.p: WOUNDED SOLDIERS.
AT THE INFIRMARY.

Mr. W. B. Randall arranged for Mr. Harri- son's. Concert Party to entertain the wounded soldiers at the Infirmary on Wednesday even- ig, the following artistes taking part:—Miss Hall (Soprano), Mr. Berry (baritone), Mr. Bes- wick (tenor), Mr. Harrison (humorist), and Mr. Williams (trombone soloist). An enjoyable concert was given, • all, the •items being well rendered. Mr. Randall, besides playing the accompaniments with taste, told some funny stories. -

div.head: CONCERT AT WHITECROSS.
div.p: CONCERT AT WHITECROSS.

Thursday week a concert was given in the above hospital, and was greatly appreciated. Miss E. Reid opened with a pianoforte solo, which was rendemd excellently. Miss E. Capel sang "A little bit of .Heaven " and "When you come home," and was loudly applauded.. Mrs. Mar- shall rendered her mandoline solos with great skill, and the ovation she received was loud and long, which was repeated for the banjo duets by herself and Mr. Whiteley. Mr. W. White, jun., who is home from France on a few days' leave, rendered "When other lips" .and "Bonny Mary of Argyle," and was much appreciated. Mr. Brobbin gave pleasing selec- tions on his concertina. Mrs. L. Monks sang "Somewhere a voice is calling" and "Annie Laurie," .and proved herself a singer of no mean ability. Mr. W. White and Mrs. Monks gave a duet, which was very enjoyable. The humour of the evening was left •to Mr. W. W. Whittle, who uphold his reputation. Miss E. Reid, at the piano, proved herself a clever player, as also did Mr. Mellor. Mr. Nolan provided cigarettes. All the arrangements of the concerts were carried out by Privates Buick und Edwards,- ,patients in the hospital. Sergeant S. E. Collins thanked the artistes and the audience showed their appreciation as soldiers can.

Another very enjoyable concert was given on Monday evening, the following contributing to the programme: Mrs. Wilson. Mr. A. E. Trow, Mr. Schofield, Mr. T. G. Bate, Sergt. Collins and Mr. E. Balmford. Billiards.

Last Saturday a billiard exhibition was given in the above hospital by Mr. Horrabin and Mr. R. Straw, and was much enjoyed. The chief breaks were 48 by Mr. Horrabin and 30 by Mr. Straw. A vote of thanks was passed on the proposition of Corporal Booth.
